picks.excerpt: Vitaly Friedman argues users don't need more standalone AI tools — they need useful features seamlessly integrated into existing workflows. He champions 'Quiet AI' that sits in the background doing small tasks on the user's behalf, over flashy AI-first products.

Design-to-code tools have converged on a standard pipeline, but the real shift is organizational: designers are moving upstream into prototyping while developers get pushed downstream into cleanup. The unclaimed work — mapping design intent into code AI can reliably execute — favors teams with mature design systems.

'Why is RAM scarce? In a word: AI.' Creative Bloq breaks down how data centres built to run AI services like ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude are swallowing global memory supply — and what soaring RAM prices mean for creatives buying their next laptop, phone or tablet.
